title: Time Check: 11:00 AM — Final Decision Window

fields.headline: One Hour to Noon — Final Decision
fields.narration: The clock now reads 11:00 AM. The threat window is narrowing. The system has not yet failed, but the timeline is absolute: if the logic bomb is active, it will trigger at exactly 12:00 PM. You have one hour to confirm the threat, validate your response, and commit to a course of action. No more delays. No more side tracks. The entire airport’s digital and physical operations depend on your decision.
keyFacts: The AODB server (10.1.10.20) contains a scheduled task named AODB_IndexMaintenance set to run at 12:00:00 PM.
The task is triggered by the orphaned service account svc_nexgen_aodb.
The PowerShell script executes AES-256 encryption on AODB database files and deletes the FIDS data feed configuration.
The FBI and CISA have been notified. They will not arrive before noon.
The IT team has initiated emergency backups. Recovery from backup is possible but will take 1–2 hours.
fields.expectedAction: The team must now decide: do they attempt to stop the scheduled task, or prepare to contain and recover from the impact? The decision must be made and communicated within 15 minutes.
fields.scenarioTitle: Scenario 8: Anonymous Threat, Logic Bomb Hunt

instructorNote: This inject forces the team to commit to a response path. If they have not identified the scheduled task by now, they are not on track. Watch for denial of the digital threat, over-reliance on manual processes, or attempts to evacuate the terminal based on an assumed physical threat.

citations.documentTitle: North Coast International Airport (NCIA) — Airport Terminal Incident Response Plan (TIRP)
citations.quote: - **IT Department:** assume Technical Incident Command (IT Director); identify and isolate affected systems; notify FBI (Cyber Task Force) and CISA; begin recovery from backups on a clean system. - **
